text:
maria: Quick decision needed: how do we handle EU PII tenants for multi-region active/active? Options: strict-resident (all traffic pinned EU) vs hybrid (writes resident, reads nearest with anonymized fallback).

sam: hybrid. strict-resident kills latency for APAC and adds a lot of infra complexity.

kai: infra cost: resident-only needs per-tenant route tables + cross-region cache priming. Rough estimate 15-30% uplift for small tenants.

maria: SLA targets: p50 <100ms, p99 <450ms for chat. If we pin everyone to EU what's the p99 impact?

sam: lab -> median +60ms for APAC, p99 +250-400ms. Strong-consistency writes to EU worsen p99 further.

devon: legal: no reads that reconstruct PII outside EU unless tenant consent and irreversible anonymization. Embeddings/hashes okay if provably irreversible and documented.

laura: ops: resident-only increases blast radius. Need runbook and fallback alerts or we'll get pages during region blips.

maria: proposed policy for RFC follow-up: enforce write residency for PII tenants (block or queue non-resident writes); allow read fallback only with tenant consent + irreversible anonymization; implement gateway header x-residency-region + tenant routing table; instrument metrics (residency.routed, residency.fallback, residency.anonymize, residency.blocked) and alert fallback >0.5% over 5m; canary opt-in for 2 tenants for 2 weeks.

sam: runtime will prototype branch residency-gate-v1; will add anonymize hook.
kai: I'll produce cost estimates and per-tenant flags.
devon: legal will draft consent wording and a short checklist.

laura: I'll write runbook pages residency-fallback, residency-priming, residency-alerts and link back.
maria: thanks all. I'll prep RFC follow-up and schedule a 30m sync tomorrow. Object now or reply in RFC.
sam: no objections.
kai: :thumbsup:
devon: :thumbsup: (pending wording)
